chapters.about: God as a shepherd and the experience of death

summary: Mrs. Abraham explores the Jewish perspective on death and comfort, using the metaphor of a game to explain how to balance living fully in the present while maintaining a connection to Hashem. She analyzes the phrase HaMakom Y'nachem Etchem and Tehillim Perek 23 to discuss how shifting one's perspective can provide comfort during times of national and personal tragedy. The class emphasizes that while the Torah focuses on instructions for life, the awareness of an afterlife serves as a background support for navigating the challenges of this world.
questions: Why do we use the word HaMakom to refer to Hashem when comforting mourners?
Why is the Torah relatively silent about the details of life after death?
How can we balance living fully in the present while keeping the goal of Olam HaBa in mind?
What does it mean to serve Hashem without expecting a reward?
How does the fear of death help us stay engaged in the game of life?
